Since \(567 = 81 \cdot 7 = 3^4 \cdot 7\), we need the order of \(10\) modulo \(81\) and modulo \(7\).

Modulo \(7\):
\[
10 \equiv 3 \pmod 7,
\]
and the order of \(3\) mod \(7\) is \(6\).

Modulo \(81\):
\[
10 = 1 + 9,
\]
so
\[
(1+9)^n \equiv 1 + 9n \pmod{81}.
\]
Thus \(10^n \equiv 1 \pmod{81}\) requires \(9n \equiv 0 \pmod{81}\), so \(n\) is divisible by \(9\). The smallest such positive \(n\) is \(9\).

Therefore, the smallest \(n\) satisfying both is
\[
\operatorname{lcm}(9,6)=18.
\]

\[
\boxed{18}
\]
